newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia PM aides say selloffs to boost '97 budget.
newsitem.headline: Latvia PM aides say selloffs to boost '97 budget.

text.p: Privatisation returns will be one of the main sources of Latvia's revenues in 1997 under the government's balanced budget proposal, top economic advisors to Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele said on Tuesday.

The two advisors, Edmund Krastinsh and Janis Platais, defended the balanced 1997 budget as parliament on Tuesday began debating its final reading. The budget is controversial as the opposition says it will hit education and welfare too much.
Krastinsh told newspaper Diena that he hoped for funds in 1997 from the sale of at least part of oil terminal Ventspils Nafta, the Latvian Shipping Company and energy firm Latvenergo.
"Therefore the contribution (from privatisation) to the budget will be the highest ever when compared with the previous and following years," Krastinsh told the newspaper.
As well as passing a balanced budget, Shkele has vowed to speed up privatisation.
A stake in the monopoly gas firm Latvian Gas has already been sold and talks are underway on Latvenergo.
Kranstinsh also strongly defended the balanced budget, which has caused controversy in a country where many people live on low wages and look to the state for support.
"A budget deficit cannot be allowed here as it can, like in Mexico, lead the state to total catastrophe," Krastinsh said.
The planned budget for 1997 comes after a planned 40 million lat deficit in 1996 and 90 million lats deficit in 1995.
Last year's deficit swelled after a banking crisis, caused by the collapse of what was the country's largest bank.
